text:
jordan: FYI new hire hit a couple of things during setup on macOS (Homebrew + zsh). Thought I'd share findings.

jordan: Steps they followed:
- `brew install redwoodctl`
- `redwoodctl install-completion --shell zsh`
- `redwoodctl auth login` (browser opens)

ivy: What happened?

jordan: Two things: 1) the `install-completion` command created `_redwoodctl` in /usr/local/share/zsh/site-functions but zsh didn't pick it up until they reloaded `~/.zshrc`. 2) more annoying: when the laptop was offline, `redwoodctl auth login` started a retry loop that re-opened the browser every ~12s. New hire ended up with 6 browser tabs to close.

noah: Oof. The completion path is a common caveat for Homebrew when using non-login shells. Docs should mention `autoload -U compinit && compinit` or `fpath` and to restart the shell.

marco: About the browser spam: current CLI auth login (browser flow) spawns a watcher that polls for the callback and attempts a local callback check. If the network is flaky it retries raw-open of the browser on certain errors. That's a bug. We should not re-open a new browser tab on every retry. Instead only open once and print the URL for manual retry.

cli-bot: New ticket created: DEVEX-5101  CLI: auth login re-opens browser on retry when offline. Assigned to @marco.

ivy: Another small thing: profiles handling. The new hire had two profiles in `~/.redwood/profiles.json` (work and personal). They ran `redwoodctl auth login --profile work` but the CLI silently merged keys into the default profile if `REDWOODCTL_PROFILE` env var was set by a sample app. Confusing.

sara: Are we reading env var precedence wrong? Expected order: explicit flag > env var > config default. If `--profile` was used, we must target that profile.

noah: I dug in: bug is in profile selection code path when the token write returns ENOENT for the target file; the code falls back to the default profile path and ignores the `--profile` flag. Patch idea: ensure atomic create of target profile file and fail with explicit error if write can't be completed, not silently fallback.

marco: I'll add a check and clearer error message. Also add a `redwoodctl config set-profile --create` helper to make new profiles explicitly.

jordan: One more repro: the starter sample app (examples/local-serve) exported `REDWOODCTL_PROFILE=default` in its `.env.example`. New hires copied it without changing and all their `redwoodctl` calls were going into the `default` profile unexpectedly. We updated the example to remove that line and add a comment about using `--profile`.

ivy: Nice catch. Docs should also show `redwoodctl whoami --profile work` and `redwoodctl auth login --device --profile work` examples. Device flow is still better for flaky connections.

cli-bot: New PR opened: https://git.redwood.internal/pulls/3056  fix(auth): stop reopening browser on retry; fix(profile): respect --profile on write.

noah: Tests: add unit for profile precedence and an integration test that simulates network failure during auth and verifies CLI does not re-open browser after first attempt.

jordan: New hire unblocked with `redwoodctl auth login --device --profile work` and removing REDWOODCTL_PROFILE from the sample `.env`. Thanks all :thumbsup:
